newsitem.title: FRANCE: Blair says in UK's interest to be part of Europe.
newsitem.headline: Blair says in UK's interest to be part of Europe.

text.p: Britain's Opposition Labour party leader Tony Blair, said on Friday it was in Britain's interest to be part of Europe and its controversial social policy.
"It is very important for Great Britain to have a constructive relationship with Europe," Blair said in an interview on French television.

Blair, was visiting to Paris for talks with conservative President Jacques Chirac, Prime Minister Alain Juppe and opposition Socialist leaders. Reuters has translated back into English the French dubbed version of his actual words.
"This doesn't mean that there won't be times when we disagree, and at those times we will speak for the British, but it is in the interests of Britain to be part of Europe."

Blair said his party, which has a big lead over Prime Minister John Major's Conservative party in the run-up to to a general election due before next May, differed with the present government on EU social legislation.

Major, who obtained an opt-out for Britain from the social chapter of the 1991 Maastricht Treaty on European Union, vowed this week to overturn an EU directive imposing a maximum 48-hour work week after the European Court of Justice ordered London to obey it.
"Our position is different," Blair said. "We believe that we should be a part of the social Europe."
On economic and monetary union, the Labour leader would not say whether he would take Britain into a single European currency.
But he said: "For us it is an economic question, Mr Major's party is completely opposed to it, but I think we have to leave our options open. We have to ask the British public."
